# ntex

> ntex is a Rust framework for composable network services: HTTP/1, HTTP/2, WebSocket, web applications, and custom protocols. Everything is a `Service<St, Req>` with a pipeline state type `St`, executed by a `Pipeline` that coordinates readiness, calls, and shutdown.

Rules for generated code:

- A service implements `call(&self, req, ctx: Ctx<'_, Self, St>)`. Call child services with `ctx.call(&self.child, req)`, never `self.child.call(...)` directly.
- A service that wraps child services must forward `bind`, `ready`, and `shutdown` to every child. Use `ntex::forward!(St, field1, field2)`; add `map_err = f` when `Self::Error` differs from the children's error. `St` is the state type parameter of the impl.
- For web middleware that only runs code before or after the inner service, use `ntex::web::middleware::from_fn(async |req, next| ...)` and call `next.call(req).await?`. No annotations are needed, except `next: Next<'_, _, MyState>` when the closure reads `next.st()`. Return `Err(web::WebError::from_err(err))` to reject a request.
- For non-web services use `ntex::service::fn_layer(async |req: Req, ctx| ...)` with explicit request, response, and error types.
- Type-inference rules for service closures: always name the error type in `fn_service`, `fn_factory`, and `fn_layer` results (`Ok::<_, MyError>(..)`); annotate the argument of closures passed to `and_then`/`then` (`.and_then(async |res: Res| ...)`), or wrap them in `fn_service`. Closures for `map`, `map_err`, `map_init_err`, and `apply_fn` need no annotations.
- Type-inference rules for web code: inside `HttpServer::new` or `test::init_service` write `App::new()`; elsewhere write `App::default()` (state `()`) or `App::<AppState<T>>::new()`. Prefer `async fn` handlers; closure handlers must annotate every argument (`async |path: web::types::Path<String>| ...`) and name the error type of `Ok(..)` results, also in `filter` closures. `?` does not convert into `WebError`; return a concrete error type that implements `WebResponseError`, or use `.map_err(web::WebError::from_err)?`. Modular config functions take `cfg: &mut web::ServiceConfig` (state `()`) or `&mut web::ServiceConfig<St>`.
- Use a `Middleware` struct plus a service with `forward!` when the middleware needs its own configuration, readiness, or a named service type.
- Write `ctx.bind(&self.child)` without a turbofish.
- Implement `bind`, `ready`, and `shutdown` by hand only when the service has extra readiness sources, such as a shared `Pipeline` (`pipeline.bind_to(&ctx)`) or a `ReadyNotifier` (`ctx.subscribe(&notifier)`).
- Async entry points use `#[ntex::main]`; async tests use `#[ntex::test]`.

## Server and client rules

- For HTTP applications, start with `web::HttpServer` and `web::App`. For custom TCP protocols or lower-level HTTP services, use `ntex::server::build()`; the standalone crate exposes the same builder as `ntex_server::net::build()`.
- Build servers inside an active ntex runtime. `server::build().bind(name, addr, SharedCfg::default(), async |state| service)` takes four arguments; `web::HttpServer::new(async |state| app).bind(addr, SharedCfg::default())` takes two. Factories are asynchronous even when construction does no asynchronous work. Call `.run().await` to wait for shutdown, not to check worker health.
- Factories run per worker and may run again after a restart. Construct `Rc`/`Cell`/`RefCell` state inside `build_with_config(async || Ok(state))`, not outside a factory that must be `Send`. Use `Arc` plus appropriate synchronization when data must be shared across workers. `SharedCfg` configures I/O and protocols; it is not application state.
- `HttpService::new(async |req| Ok(..))` needs an explicit error type (`Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(..)`). A named `async fn` with a concrete return type avoids this annotation. Finish response builders with `.build()`, not `.finish()`.
- For simple sequential protocols use `Io::recv(&codec)` and `Io::send(item, &codec)`. `BytesCodec` yields available byte chunks, not application-message boundaries. Use a framing codec for message protocols.
- `Dispatcher::new(io, codec, pipeline)` requires a `Pipeline` whose service accepts `DispatchItem<Codec>` and returns `Result<Option<EncodedItem>, E>`. Match `Item` separately from `Control`/`Stop` notifications; `Ok(None)` emits no response.
- Service factories for `server::test_server`, `http::test::server`, and `web::test::server` take `async |_| service_or_app`, with `&()` as the argument. `server::TestServerBuilder::with(cfg, factory)` passes `&Cfg::State` to the service factory. State-initialization closures remain zero-argument: `async || Ok(state)`. Use the test server's address, not a fixed port.
- Client send/body errors do not automatically convert into `std::io::Error`. Use a concrete application error or `Result<_, Box<dyn std::error::Error>>` to preserve them with `?`. If only a message is needed, explicitly use `.map_err(|err| std::io::Error::other(err.to_string()))?`; this loses the original error and diagnostic context. Do not require `Send + Sync` on the boxed error: client errors can be worker-local.
- TLS belongs in connection setup, not protocol logic. Compose acceptors/connectors with services over `Io`; use generic filters, `seal()`, or `boxed()` to keep protocol code independent of TLS backends.
- HTTP clients use `openssl`, `rustls`, or `secure_connector` for HTTPS; `ClientBuilder::connector` configures unsecured connections. Supply verifying TLS configurations explicitly: the built-in OpenSSL HTTP-client default currently disables certificate verification.
- `WsClient` needs an explicit TLS connector even for `wss://`: use `openssl`, `rustls`, or `connector`, and offer HTTP/1.1 rather than h2. Server-side WebSocket handlers work unchanged behind an HTTPS listener.
- Read peer certificates with `PeerCertDer` / `PeerCertChainDer`, then parse with `x509::PeerCerts`. Certificate presence or parsing is not trust verification or authorization. Schannel's `request_client_cert(true)` neither requires a certificate nor validates its trust; reject missing/untrusted identities before protected handling.
- See the [TLS guide](https://docs.ntex.rs/10-tls.html) and [runnable TLS examples](https://github.com/ntex-rs/examples/tree/main/tls) for backend, component, identity, and mutual-authentication configuration.

## Testing rules

- Test the application the server runs. Register routes in `fn config(cfg: &mut web::ServiceConfig)` (or `&mut web::ServiceConfig<St>`), call `App::new().configure(config)` in both `main` and the tests, and keep tests in `#[cfg(test)] mod tests` at the bottom of the file.
- Prefer in-process tests: `web::test::init_service(App::new()...)` with `TestRequest` and `call_service` opens no socket. Use `init_service_st(state.clone(), App::<St>::new()...)` for stateful apps and keep a clone of shared handles to inspect state.
- Use a real server (`web::test::server`, `http::test::server`, `server::test_server`) only for WebSocket, streaming, client, TLS, or connection behavior; it binds an available port. Never use fixed ports, external services, or sleeps for synchronization.
- Test a `Service` directly with `Pipeline::new(state, service).call(req).await`. Test codecs and `Io` protocols in memory with `ntex::io::testing::IoTest`.
- Assert the status and the body; for failures, assert the status code a client sees. Use `read_body` for bytes and `read_response_json` for JSON.

## Templates

Function service executed by a pipeline:

```rust
use ntex::service::{Pipeline, fn_service};

let service = fn_service(async |req: u32| Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(req + 1));
let pipeline = Pipeline::new((), service);
assert_eq!(pipeline.call(1).await?, 2);
```

Minimal web server:

```rust
use ntex::{SharedCfg, web};

#[web::get("/")]
async fn index() -> &'static str {
    "Hello world!"
}

#[ntex::main]
async fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    web::HttpServer::new(async |_| web::App::new().service(index))
        .bind("127.0.0.1:8080", SharedCfg::new("hello-world"))?
        .run()
        .await
}
```

Closure web middleware (preferred):

```rust
use ntex::http::header::{HeaderName, HeaderValue};
use ntex::web::{self, App, HttpResponse, middleware::from_fn};

web::HttpServer::new(async |_| {
    App::new()
        .middleware(from_fn(async |req, next| {
            if !req.headers().contains_key("authorization") {
                return Ok(req.into_response(HttpResponse::Unauthorized().build()));
            }
            let mut res = next.call(req).await?;
            res.headers_mut().insert(
                HeaderName::from_static("x-application"),
                HeaderValue::from_static("example"),
            );
            Ok(res)
        }))
        .route("/", web::get().to(async || "Hello"))
});
```

Struct middleware with forwarding:

```rust
use std::time::Instant;

use ntex::web::{WebRequest, WebResponse};
use ntex::{Ctx, Middleware, Service};

pub struct Timing;

pub struct TimingService<S> {
    service: S,
}

impl<S, St> Middleware<S, St> for Timing {
    type Service = TimingService<S>;

    fn create(&self, _: &St, service: S) -> Self::Service {
        TimingService { service }
    }
}

impl<S, St, ReqSt> Service<St, WebRequest<ReqSt>> for TimingService<S>
where
    S: Service<St, WebRequest<ReqSt>, Res = WebResponse>,
{
    type Res = WebResponse;
    type Error = S::Error;

    ntex::forward!(St, service);

    async fn call(
        &self,
        req: WebRequest<ReqSt>,
        ctx: Ctx<'_, Self, St>,
    ) -> Result<WebResponse, S::Error> {
        let start = Instant::now();
        let res = ctx.call(&self.service, req).await;
        log::info!("request took {:?}", start.elapsed());
        res
    }
}
```

Several children with error conversion:

```rust
use ntex::{Ctx, Service};

pub enum AuthError<E> {
    Denied,
    Service(E),
}

pub struct Authorized<A, S> {
    check: A,
    service: S,
}

impl<A, S, St, Req> Service<St, Req> for Authorized<A, S>
where
    A: Service<St, Req, Res = (Req, bool), Error = S::Error>,
    S: Service<St, Req>,
{
    type Res = S::Res;
    type Error = AuthError<S::Error>;

    ntex::forward!(St, check, service, map_err = AuthError::Service);

    async fn call(&self, req: Req, ctx: Ctx<'_, Self, St>) -> Result<S::Res, Self::Error> {
        let (req, allowed) = ctx.call(&self.check, req).await.map_err(AuthError::Service)?;
        if !allowed {
            return Err(AuthError::Denied);
        }
        ctx.call(&self.service, req).await.map_err(AuthError::Service)
    }
}
```

Explicit forwarding with a shared pipeline child:

```rust
use ntex::service::{BindCtx, Ctx, Pipeline, Service};

pub struct Cached<S, E> {
    service: S,
    // shared with other services, owned and shut down elsewhere
    cache: Pipeline<String, Option<String>, E>,
}

impl<S, St, E> Service<St, String> for Cached<S, E>
where
    S: Service<St, String, Res = String, Error = E>,
    E: 'static,
{
    type Res = String;
    type Error = E;

    fn bind(&self, ctx: BindCtx<'_>) {
        ctx.bind(&self.service);
        self.cache.bind_to(&ctx);
    }

    async fn ready(&self, ctx: Ctx<'_, Self, St>) -> Result<(), E> {
        self.cache.ready().await?;
        ctx.ready(&self.service).await
    }

    async fn shutdown(&self, ctx: Ctx<'_, Self, St>) {
        // the shared cache pipeline is shut down by its owner
        ctx.shutdown(&self.service).await;
    }

    async fn call(&self, req: String, ctx: Ctx<'_, Self, St>) -> Result<String, E> {
        if let Some(res) = self.cache.call(req.clone()).await? {
            return Ok(res);
        }
        ctx.call(&self.service, req).await
    }
}
```

TCP byte-echo server:

```rust
use ntex::{SharedCfg, codec::BytesCodec, io::Io, service::fn_service};

async fn echo(io: Io) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    while let Some(msg) = io.recv(&BytesCodec).await? {
        io.send(msg, &BytesCodec).await?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

#[ntex::main]
async fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    ntex::server::build()
        .bind("echo", "127.0.0.1:8080", SharedCfg::default(), async |_| fn_service(echo))?
        .run()
        .await
}
```

Dispatcher-based byte-echo server (control and stop notifications need no response here):

```rust
use ntex::codec::BytesCodec;
use ntex::io::{DispatchItem, Dispatcher, Io};
use ntex::service::{Pipeline, fn_service};

async fn serve(io: Io) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    let handler = fn_service(async |item: DispatchItem<BytesCodec>| match item {
        DispatchItem::Item(frame) => Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(Some(frame)),
        _ => Ok(None),
    });
    Dispatcher::new(io, BytesCodec, Pipeline::new((), handler)).await
}

#[ntex::main]
async fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    ntex::server::build()
        .bind("echo", "127.0.0.1:8080", ntex::SharedCfg::default(), async |_| fn_service(serve))?
        .run()
        .await
}
```

Low-level HTTP server without `web::App`:

```rust
use ntex::SharedCfg;
use ntex::http::{HttpService, Request, Response};

async fn handle(req: Request) -> Result<Response, std::io::Error> {
    Ok(Response::Ok().body(format!("path: {}", req.path())))
}

#[ntex::main]
async fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    ntex::server::build()
        .bind("http", "127.0.0.1:8080", SharedCfg::default(), async |_| HttpService::new(handle))?
        .run()
        .await
}
```

Network test with `test_server` and `Client`:

```rust
use ntex::client::Client;
use ntex::http::{HttpService, Response};

#[ntex::test]
async fn http_roundtrip() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let srv = ntex::server::test_server(async |_| {
        HttpService::new(async |_| Ok::<_, std::io::Error>(Response::Ok().body("hello")))
    });
    let url = format!("http://{}/", srv.addr());
    let res = Client::new().get(url.as_str()).send().await?;
    assert!(res.status().is_success());
    assert_eq!(res.body().await?, "hello");
    Ok(())
}
```

In-process route test that uses the application's config:

```rust
use ntex::http::StatusCode;
use ntex::web::{self, App, HttpResponse, test};
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};

#[derive(Debug, PartialEq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
struct User {
    name: String,
}

async fn create(user: web::types::Json<User>) -> HttpResponse {
    HttpResponse::Created().json(&user.into_inner())
}

pub fn config(cfg: &mut web::ServiceConfig) {
    cfg.route("/users", web::post().to(create));
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;

    #[ntex::test]
    async fn create_user() {
        let app = test::init_service(App::new().configure(config)).await;

        let user = User { name: "alice".into() };
        let req = test::TestRequest::post().uri("/users").json(&user).to_request();
        let res = test::call_service(&app, req).await;
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::CREATED);
        let body: User = serde_json::from_slice(&test::read_body(res).await).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(body, user);

        let req = test::TestRequest::post().uri("/users").header("content-type", "application/json").payload("{").to_request();
        let res = test::call_service(&app, req).await;
        assert_eq!(res.status(), StatusCode::BAD_REQUEST);
    }
}
```

Stateful route test (keep a clone of the shared handle to inspect state):

```rust
use std::{cell::Cell, rc::Rc};

use ntex::web::{self, App, AppState, test};

type Hits = AppState<Rc<Cell<usize>>>;

async fn hit(hits: &Hits, (): ()) -> String {
    hits.set(hits.get() + 1);
    hits.get().to_string()
}

pub fn config(cfg: &mut web::ServiceConfig<Hits>) {
    cfg.route("/hit", web::post().to_with_state(hit));
}

#[ntex::test]
async fn counts_hits() {
    let hits = Hits::default();
    let app = test::init_service_st(hits.clone(), App::<Hits>::new().configure(config)).await;

    for expected in ["1", "2"] {
        let req = test::TestRequest::post().uri("/hit").to_request();
        let res = test::call_service(&app, req).await;
        assert!(res.status().is_success());
        assert_eq!(test::read_body(res).await, expected);
    }
    assert_eq!(hits.get(), 2);
}
```

WebSocket test against a real test server:

```rust
use ntex::util::Bytes;
use ntex::web::{self, App, HttpRequest, test, ws};

async fn echo(frame: ws::Frame) -> Result<Option<ws::Message>, std::io::Error> {
    Ok(match frame {
        ws::Frame::Text(text) => Some(ws::Message::Text(String::from_utf8_lossy(&text).as_ref().into())),
        ws::Frame::Ping(msg) => Some(ws::Message::Pong(msg)),
        ws::Frame::Close(reason) => Some(ws::Message::Close(reason)),
        _ => None,
    })
}

async fn socket(req: HttpRequest) {
    let _ = ws::start(&req, None, echo).await;
}

#[ntex::test]
async fn ws_echo() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let srv = test::server(async |_| App::new().route("/ws", web::get().to(socket)));
    let (io, codec, _) = srv.ws_at("/ws").await?.into_inner();

    io.send(ws::Message::Text("hello".into()), &codec).await?;
    assert_eq!(io.recv(&codec).await?, Some(ws::Frame::Text(Bytes::from_static(b"hello"))));
    Ok(())
}
```

Protocol test without sockets, for `echo` from the TCP byte-echo template:

```rust
use ntex::io::testing::IoTest;

#[ntex::test]
async fn echo_in_memory() {
    let (client, server) = IoTest::create();
    client.remote_buffer_cap(1024);
    let _task = ntex::rt::spawn(echo(Io::from(server)));

    client.write(b"ping");
    assert_eq!(client.read().await.unwrap(), b"ping"[..]);
}
```

Worker-local state (counts accepted connections, then closes them):

```rust
use std::{cell::Cell, rc::Rc};

use ntex::{SharedCfg, io::Io};

#[derive(Clone, Default)]
struct Connections(Rc<Cell<usize>>);

async fn handle(st: &Connections, _io: Io) -> std::io::Result<()> {
    st.0.set(st.0.get() + 1);
    Ok(())
}

#[ntex::main]
async fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    ntex::server::build_with_config(async || Ok(Connections::default()))
        .bind("svc", "127.0.0.1:8080", SharedCfg::default(), async |_| ntex::service(handle))?
        .run()
        .await
}
```

## Coming from actix-web

| actix-web | ntex |
|---|---|
| `#[actix_web::main]`, `#[actix_web::test]` | `#[ntex::main]`, `#[ntex::test]` |
| `HttpServer::new(\|\| App::new())` | `web::HttpServer::new(async \|_\| App::new())` or `web::server(..)` |
| `.bind(("127.0.0.1", 8080))?` | `.bind("127.0.0.1:8080", SharedCfg::default())?` |
| `.wrap(m)` | `.middleware(m)` on `App`, `Scope`, `Resource` |
| `middleware::from_fn`, `wrap_fn` | `web::middleware::from_fn(async \|req, next\| next.call(req).await)` |
| `middleware::{Logger, DefaultHeaders, Compress}` | same names in `web::middleware` (`Compress` needs feature `compress`) |
| `web::Data<T>` + `.app_data(..)` | `web::AppState<T>` from `web::server_with_config(async \|\| Ok(AppState::new(v)), ..)`, read by handlers registered with `.to_with_state(h)` where `async fn h(st: &AppState<T>, (): (), ..)` |
| `web::Json/Path/Query/Form/Payload` | `web::types::Json/Path/Query/Form/Payload` |
| `Bytes`, `Either` | `ntex::util::Bytes`, `ntex::util::Either` |
| `ResponseError` | `web::WebResponseError<St, web::DefaultError>` with `fn error_response(&self, st: &St) -> HttpResponse`; type must impl `std::error::Error` |
| `actix_web::Error` | `web::WebError`; `?` does not convert, use `.map_err(web::WebError::from_err)?` |
| `HttpResponse::Ok().finish()` | `HttpResponse::Ok().build()`; `.json(&value)` takes a reference |
| `ServiceRequest`, `ServiceResponse` | `web::WebRequest`, `web::WebResponse` |
| `#[get("/")]` | `#[web::get("/")]` |
| `actix_web::rt::spawn` | `ntex::rt::spawn` |
| `actix_web::test::*` | `ntex::web::test::{init_service, call_service, read_body, TestRequest}` |

`scope`, `resource`, `route`, `service`, `to`, `configure`, `ServiceConfig` and `default_service` keep their actix-web names.

## Guide

- [Service Model](https://docs.ntex.rs/1-service.html): the `Service` trait, factories, and function services
- [Service Pipelines](https://docs.ntex.rs/2-pipeline.html): readiness, binding, forwarding, and shutdown
- [Service State](https://docs.ntex.rs/3-state.html)
- [Runtime](https://docs.ntex.rs/4-runtime.html)
- [Server](https://docs.ntex.rs/5-server.html)
- [Worker and Request State](https://docs.ntex.rs/6-server-app.html)
- [I/O Abstraction Layer](https://docs.ntex.rs/7-io.html)
- [Applications and Routing](https://docs.ntex.rs/8.1-web-app.html)
- [Application State](https://docs.ntex.rs/8.2-web-app.html)
- [Filters and Middleware](https://docs.ntex.rs/8.3-web-app.html)
- [Extractors and Responders](https://docs.ntex.rs/8.4-web-app.html)
- [Error Handling](https://docs.ntex.rs/8.5-web-app.html)
- [WebSocket Support](https://docs.ntex.rs/8.6-web-app.html)
- [Byte Buffers](https://docs.ntex.rs/9-bytes.html)
- [Securing Connections with TLS](https://docs.ntex.rs/10-tls.html): backend and component configuration, identities, peer certificates, and mutual authentication
- [Making HTTP Requests](https://docs.ntex.rs/13-client.html): the `ntex::client` HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 client, connection pooling, `ClientConfig` and timeouts, TLS connectors, request bodies, reading responses, and client middleware
- [Timers and Time Utilities](https://docs.ntex.rs/12-time.html): timer wheel design and precision, `Millis` and `Seconds`, `sleep`, `deadline`, `timeout`, `interval`, and callback timers

## API

- [ntex](https://docs.ntex.rs/api/ntex/index.html)
- [ntex_service](https://docs.ntex.rs/api/ntex_service/index.html): `Service`, `Middleware`, `Pipeline`, `forward!`, `fn_layer`
- [ntex::web](https://docs.ntex.rs/api/ntex/web/index.html): `App`, `HttpServer`, `middleware::from_fn`
- [ntex_server::net](https://docs.ntex.rs/api/ntex_server/net/index.html): `build`, `build_with_config`, `ServerBuilder`, `test_server`
- [ntex::tls](https://docs.ntex.rs/api/ntex/tls/index.html): acceptors, connectors, `TlsConfig`, and portable `x509` identities and trust
